content: Before inserting an image into a chapter on WikiDoc, it is mandatory to upload the image to the WikiDoc server. Images can only be added to a WikiDoc page if they are already stored on the server. If the image you wish to use is not yet uploaded, you must complete the uploading process. To do this, navigate to the upload page by either clicking on Upload file or searching for Special:Upload on WikiDoc. This page provides detailed instructions for uploading an image to the server. On the upload page, you will encounter two fields. In the Source file name field, click the Browse button to locate the image file on your computer's hard drive. In the Destination file name field, type the name you want the image to have on WikiDoc. It is crucial to use a descriptive name for the image, as this will facilitate its discovery and indexing by search engines. Choose a name that aligns with the search terms you would use to find the image. Once the fields are completed, click the Upload file button. After uploading, the image will appear on the server. It is recommended to copy the file name for later use when inserting the image into a WikiDoc page. Once an image is uploaded to the server, it can be inserted into multiple pages. The file names of uploaded images can be found in the Image file list or the Gallery of new images on WikiDoc. Knowing the file name is essential for inserting the image into a page. To insert an image into a WikiDoc page, you must use specific image code. This is done in the editing window of the page you are working on. Access the editing panel by selecting the Edit this page tab at the top of the page. Before placing the image code, determine the optimal location for the image. Consider how the text will wrap around the image. For instance, placing the image at the start of a section often looks best. To do this, leave an empty line immediately above or below the section heading and type the image code. The extra line will not affect the final output, apart from positioning the image. After inserting the image code, click the Show preview button at the bottom of the editing window to view the reformatted page. If the image is aligned to the left or right, the text will wrap around it. If the image is centered or has no alignment specified, the text will appear below the image. Adjust the placement as needed until the layout is satisfactory. Once finalized, click the Save page button to save your changes. Most images on the WikiDoc server are too large to display at their full size. Therefore, resizing is often necessary. Additionally, the server requires information about the image's placement, frame type, and whether a caption is needed. To streamline this process, it is recommended to use a standard format that includes all basic options. Examples of this syntax can be found in the Examples section of the WikiDoc image use policy. When specifying the type of image display, the following options are available: Thumbnail or thumb: The image is scaled down to a default width of 180 pixels (or a user-specified width) and enclosed in a box. If a caption is provided, it will appear below the image. By default, the image is aligned to the right unless overridden by the Location attribute. Frame: The image retains its original size and is enclosed in a box. If a caption is provided, it will appear below the image. No specification: The image retains its original size without a border. Captions, if provided, will not be displayed. Border: Similar to no specification, but a border is added around the image. For image placement, the following options are available: Right: The image and its box are placed on the right side of the page, with the text wrapping around it. Left: The image and its box are placed on the left side of the page, with the text wrapping around it. Center: The image and its box are centered on the page, with the text appearing below it. None: The image and its box are placed on the left side of the page, with the text appearing below it. To adjust the size of an image, you can specify dimensions such as 100px (width of 100 pixels) or 100x200px (maximum width of 100 pixels and maximum height of 200 pixels). The image will maintain its original aspect ratio. If the image is smaller than the specified dimensions, it will remain at its original size. Captions can be added to images by including text that is not identified as an image attribute. Additional formatting options, such as bold or italic text, can be applied to captions. For advanced image syntax, options such as alignment, size, thumbnail, frame, and alternate text can be combined using vertical bars (|). The syntax is backward compatible, meaning older articles do not need to be updated. If multiple unknown options are included, the last one will take precedence. To create a gallery of images, specific markup can be used to display multiple images in a grid format. For example, you can configure the gallery to display three images per row. To prevent text from wrapping around an image, use markup to cancel the floating effect. This is particularly useful for aesthetic reasons or when transitioning to a new topic. To align a gallery to the left or right and allow text to float around it, use specific code. For instance, you can compare images of normal arterioles, hypertensive arterioles, and arterioles in a patient with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). If you want to link to a page with a detailed description of an image, use a leading colon before image: in the intra-wiki link. This will create a hyperlink to the image's description page.
